text: Only collision estimators shall search for recycled parts. Users without the collision estimator role shall not have access to the search for recycled parts.
rationale: Restringe el acceso a la busqueda de partes recicladas a un rol autorizado, es decir, limita quien puede ver informacion.

text: The product shall have audit capabilities.The product shall store messages for a minimum of one year for audit and transaction tracking purposes.
rationale: Exige capacidades de auditoria y conservar mensajes para auditoria y seguimiento de transacciones, sin mencionar pruebas ante disputas.

text: All additions of new users and modifications to user\92s access shall be recorded on the User Report.
rationale: Exige registrar en un reporte las altas de usuarios y los cambios de acceso, lo que permite rastrear cambios.

text: The product shall provide players no access to information that might reveal the identity of another player
rationale: Impide el acceso a informacion que revele la identidad de otro jugador, es decir, protege la privacidad.

text: Only adjusters with a supervisor role can update preferred repair facility ratings. Users without the supervisor role cannot access the repair facility ratings.
rationale: Solo el rol supervisor puede actualizar las calificaciones (integridad) y los demas no pueden acceder a ellas (confidencialidad).

text: The system’s back-end servers shall never display a customer’s password. The customer’s password may be reset but never shown.
rationale: Prohibe mostrar la contrasena del cliente, protegiendo un dato sensible frente a divulgacion.

text: The system shall be built such that it is as secure as possible from malicious interference.
rationale: Pide seguridad frente a interferencia maliciosa, lo que corresponde a resistir ataques.

text: The website shall protect itself from intentional abuse and notify the administrator at all occurrences.
rationale: Exige protegerse del abuso intencional y notificar al administrador, es decir, resistir y detectar ataques.

text: The product shall ensure that only company employees or external users with company-approved user IDs may have product access. 100% of all logons shall be by either company employees or external users with company-approved user IDs.
rationale: Exige que solo empleados o externos con IDs aprobados puedan ingresar, lo que implica verificar la identidad del usuario.

text: The system shall use secure sockets in all transactions that include any confidential customer information.
rationale: Exige canales seguros (sockets seguros) para transacciones con informacion confidencial del cliente.

text: Only managers are able to perform search queries for reservations by user. 100% of all search queries for reservations by user shall be from logons of only management logons.
rationale: Limita las consultas de reservas por usuario a cuentas de gerencia, restringiendo quien puede ver informacion.

text: Everyone (stakeholders and guests) can have access to the system and the catalogue. Every client must have secure and private access to his/her data. The and the service man can have access to every part of the system. All these accesses (except the “guest tour” access) require identification through ID and password.
rationale: Exige acceso seguro y privado a los datos del cliente (confidencialidad) e identificacion mediante ID y contrasena (autenticidad).

text: A tablet shall require a user to log in using a username and password.
rationale: Exige que el usuario inicie sesion con usuario y contrasena, es decir, autenticacion.

text: Full data backups must be created daily.
rationale: Los respaldos diarios son disponibilidad y recuperacion no maliciosa, que no es subcaracteristica de seguridad segun la guia.

text: The Disputes application shall ensure that only authorized users are allowed to logon to the application.
rationale: Exige que solo usuarios autorizados puedan iniciar sesion, lo que implica verificar su identidad al ingresar.

text: The product shall ensure that the database\92s data corresponds to the data entered by the user. Each conference room reservation in the system will contain the same information as was entered by the user.
rationale: Exige que los datos almacenados correspondan exactamente a los ingresados por el usuario, es decir, exactitud y no alteracion.

text: The website must provide highest degree of security to the registered users. All the transactions that are made must be secured. The sensitive information passed to and from the website must be secured. Identity theft and other security related issues must be solved. Unauthorized transmission of sensitive information of the user to third party websites for reference must be avoided. On the basis of user agreement the information must be processed. All the information about the registered user must be securely stored in the central database.
rationale: Exige proteger la informacion sensible del usuario en transito y almacenada y evitar su transmision no autorizada a terceros, es decir, privacidad.

text: Only valid data shall be entered into the system. No invalid data shall be entered into the system.
rationale: Exige validar que solo datos validos entren al sistema, lo que corresponde a exactitud y coherencia de los datos.

text: A waiter that attempts to log into a second tablet while already logged into another tablet shall be rejected and notified through both tablets.
rationale: Rechaza un segundo inicio de sesion simultaneo del mismo mesero, lo que se relaciona con el control de la identidad de la sesion, sin mencionar un ataque.

text: A customer can only stream a movie if they purchased it and are within the 2 day viewing period.
rationale: Restringe el acceso al contenido a quien lo compro y dentro del periodo permitido, lo que es un control de acceso aunque cercano a una regla funcional.

text: Only authorized users shall have access to the portion of the system that interfaces with CampusConnect.
rationale: Limita el acceso a una parte del sistema a usuarios autorizados.

text: The system shall not leave any cookies on the customer’s computer containing the user’s password.
rationale: Prohibe dejar cookies con la contrasena del usuario, evitando exponer datos sensibles.

text: Unauthorised users can only read data without modifying anything.
rationale: Limita a los usuarios no autorizados a solo lectura, impidiendo que modifiquen datos.

text: Personal information security is defined outside the scope of the SDMS by the database server.
rationale: Declara la seguridad de informacion personal fuera del alcance del sistema, por lo que no impone un requisito concreto.

text: The product shall ensure that only supervisors can view schedule of all callers.The product must ensure that supervisors are allowed to access advertise empty time slots.
rationale: Restringe a los supervisores la visualizacion de los horarios de todos los llamantes, limitando quien puede ver informacion.

text: The system shall automatically log out all customers after a period of inactivity.
rationale: El cierre automatico por inactividad limita la exposicion y el abuso de sesiones, segun la regla 7.

text: The IP addresses where the transaction was made from will be logged.
rationale: Exige registrar las direcciones IP de origen de las transacciones, lo que permite rastrear de donde provino cada accion.

text: Users shall be required to log into the system for all operations except the operations on the login page.
rationale: Exige iniciar sesion para casi todas las operaciones, es decir, autenticacion del usuario.

text: The System shall granularly control access rights to all major subsystems. It should be possible to assign access rights to all subsystems independently.
rationale: Exige control granular de derechos de acceso por subsistema, lo que limita quien puede ver y modificar, aunque no precisa el tipo de acceso.

text: The product shall ensure that only supervisors can advertise empty time slots.The product must ensure that supervisors are allowed to access advertise empty time slots.
rationale: Restricts to supervisors the ability to publish time slots, which limits who can create or modify data.

text: All credit card information will be secured on the server and only accessible by authorized Izogn administrators. Information will be encrypted in the database.
rationale: Credit card data is encrypted and accessible only to authorized administrators, protecting it from disclosure.

text: The system shall only be accessed by authorized Corporate Community Grants (CCR) employees. Users must be authenticated using their IBM intranet user name and password.
rationale: Access is limited to authorized employees who must authenticate with user name and password.

text: System security and access levels are provided in the online system. There are varying levels of system access and functional authority. Each student’s access is limited to his/her own registration records. Only authorized system administrator(s) has access to all student registration records.
rationale: Students can access only their own records and only administrators can access all records, restricting information access.

text: The WCS system shall not allow automatic logins by any user. Cookies containing WCS login information about a user will not be stored on a user\92s computer.
rationale: Prohibits automatic logins and storing login information in cookies, protecting credentials and requiring explicit authentication.

text: The product shall ensure that it can only be accessed by authorized users. The product will be able to distinguish between authorized and unauthorized users in all access attempts
rationale: Only authorized users may access the product and it must distinguish authorized from unauthorized users on each attempt.

text: All users of the system shall login using some form of unique identification.
rationale: Requires all users to log in with unique identification, which is user identification/authentication.

text: A display shall not require a user to log in.
rationale: States that no login is required, so it expresses no security subcharacteristic.

text: System will use secured database
rationale: Generic 'secured database' statement without explicit access, encryption or attack details.

text: User access should be limited to the permissions granted to their role(s) Each level in the PCG hierarchy will be assigned a role and users will be assigned to these roles. Access to functionality within RFS system is dependent on the privileges/permission assigned to the role..
rationale: Role-based permissions limit which users may access and operate functionality, covering read and modify rights.

text: A waiter password used for tablet login must be changed every three months.
rationale: Password policy (periodic change) for tablet login concerns credential-based authentication.

text: The Disputes System shall generate a User Report that details any new users that have been added and any changes to an existing user\92s access level. The report will be reviewed for auditing purposes.
rationale: Report of added users and access-level changes reviewed for auditing traces who changed what.

text: The website shall make its user aware of its information practices before collection data from them via a Privacy Policy accessible on all pages of the website.
rationale: Privacy policy about data collection practices relates to privacy of personal data.

text: Only authorized personnel can access sales information.
rationale: Restricts access to sales information to authorized personnel.

text: The Commissioner will be the only authorized user per league to adjust league settings.
rationale: Only the Commissioner may change league settings, restricting who can modify data.

text: The system shall have basic data integrity checking to reduce the possibility of incorrect or invalid data being introduced.
rationale: Data integrity checking to prevent incorrect or invalid data being introduced.

text: Only authorized users shall have access to clinical site information.
rationale: Access to clinical site information is limited to authorized users.

text: Logout must be automatic after 1 hour of inactivity.
rationale: Automatic logout after inactivity limits session exposure to misuse (rule 7).

text: The application must log the user out when it is exited.
rationale: Logging the user out on exit ends the session and limits exposure to misuse of an open session.

text: The system shall notify customers of changes to its information policy.
rationale: Notifying customers of information policy changes concerns privacy practices for their data.

text: All authorized users once authenticated must be able to logon to the Disputes System
rationale: Users must be authenticated before logging on to the system.

text: Only users with Update access must be able to initiate dispute requests.
rationale: Only users with Update access may initiate dispute requests, restricting who can create data.

text: Each team owner will need to use a username and password in order to be authenticated to reach the team owner\92s page
rationale: Team owners must authenticate with username and password.

text: The System shall maintain consistent security. Any changes in user passwords and/or permissions should take affect in all parts of the System.
rationale: Requires password and permission changes to be applied consistently across the system, mostly concerning credentials.

text: The system must automatically log out all customers after a period of inactivity.
rationale: Automatic logout after inactivity limits the exposure of idle sessions to abuse (rule 7).

text: Fit Criterion: Dr Susan Poslusny and Karen Sysol are the only people who shall have access to the final class section scheduling for the system that interfaces with CampusConnect.
rationale: Only two named people may access the final class section scheduling.

text: A surface computer shall not require a user to log in.
rationale: States that no login is required, so it expresses no security subcharacteristic.

text: System will use secured database.
rationale: Generic 'secured database' statement without explicit access, encryption or attack details.

text: All the passwords that are generated or accepted must be stored in database in an encrypted form.
rationale: Passwords must be stored encrypted, protecting sensitive data from disclosure.

text: To prevent attacks the system should generate random word and ask the user to enter it correctly for multiple tryings.
rationale: A random-word challenge is meant explicitly to prevent attacks (automated or repeated attempts).

text: User authentication and privileges are defined outside the scope of the sytem by the Microsoft Active Directroy Server.
rationale: User authentication is delegated to Active Directory, so it only weakly refers to authenticating users.

text: The product shall ensure that only supervisors can enter a caller\92s schedule.The product must ensure that supervisors are allowed to access advertise empty time slots.
rationale: Restricting who can enter schedules limits modification (Integrity) and restricting who can access time slots limits reading (Confidentiality).

text: The product shall have security.The product shall provide authentication and authorization.
rationale: Requires authentication (Authenticity); authorization is mentioned without saying what is protected.

text: Only registered realtors shall be able to access the system.
rationale: Restricts system access to registered realtors, an access restriction to authorized users.

text: Only authorized user shall access the RFS system. ONLY users that exist in the UAS system with the RFS system assigned to their role(s) shall access the RFS system and use it.
rationale: Only authorized users with the right role may access the system, an access restriction.

text: All network transactions that involve financial information or personally identifiable information shall be encrypted.
rationale: Encryption of financial and personal data in transit protects against disclosure.

text: Patrons shall log in according to the restricted computer system access policy.
rationale: Requires patrons to log in, i.e. to authenticate.

text: Only users who have been authorized for home access to the corporate Intranet may use the COS from non-company locations.
rationale: Limits remote use of the system to users authorized for home access, an access restriction.

text: A waiter password used for tablet login must have a bit-strength of at least 64 bits.
rationale: Password strength for tablet login concerns credential-based authentication.

text: A waiter shall only be able to log into one tablet at any given instance of time.
rationale: Limits a waiter's login to a single tablet, a constraint on identity/session use in authentication.

text: Secure data transfer over the Internet could be provided using SSL encryption that will be configured by the host system administrator.
rationale: SSL encryption provides secure data transfer, protecting data from disclosure.

text: Sensitive data will be encrypted before being sent over insecure connections like the internet.
rationale: Sensitive data must be encrypted before transmission over insecure connections.

text: The system will develop a security system that will reduce to the minimum the possibility of corruption from systems and/or humans.
rationale: Aims to minimize corruption of the system by systems or humans, which relates to protecting data/programs from alteration.

text: System will have different types of users and every user has access constraints.
rationale: Per-user-type access constraints restrict who can access information, without specifying read versus modify.

text: The data transaction between client and server must be encrypted using SSL technology.
rationale: Client-server transactions must be encrypted with SSL, a confidentiality measure.

text: The system shall utilize HTTPS communication to ensure data confidentiality.
rationale: HTTPS is required explicitly to ensure data confidentiality.

text: The customer’s web browser shall never display a customer’s credit card number after retrieving from the database. It shall always be shown with just the last 4 digits of the credit card number.
rationale: Masking the credit card number to its last 4 digits prevents disclosure of sensitive data.

text: The system shall use the organization\92s standard virus protection software to help monitor threats to itself.
rationale: Virus protection software monitors threats, i.e. detects and resists malware.

text: The Disputes application shall ensure that only users with the appropriate access level are allowed to initiate dispute requests.
rationale: Only users with the appropriate access level may initiate (create) dispute requests, restricting who can create data.

text: The Disputes application shall manipulate and view business data. Users will not have direct access to data files or databases.
rationale: Denying users direct access to data files and databases protects data from unauthorized reading and modification.

text: Successful authentication is a prerequisite for the processing of any on-line or offline CEPS transaction
rationale: Successful authentication is required before any transaction is processed.

text: On-line authentication must take place between the card issuer and the CEP card for load, unload, and currency exchange transactions
rationale: Requires on-line authentication between the issuer and the card for transactions.

text: The card issuer and the CEP card share a secret key to generate and verify MACs
rationale: A shared secret key to generate and verify MACs supports detecting alteration and verifying the origin of messages.

text: Off-line authentication must take place between a PSAM in the POS device and the CEP card for purchase and cancel last purchase transactions
rationale: Requires off-line authentication between the PSAM and the card.

text: The card and the PSAM must use a public key algorithm for mutual authentication and session key exchange, as no permanent shared secret key may exist between the CEP card and the PSAM
rationale: Mutual authentication with a public key algorithm between card and PSAM.

text: To load value into a slot of the CEP card securely, the load device establishes a connection between the issuer and the CEP card
rationale: Says the load is done securely via an issuer connection but states no specific security property, so no subcharacteristic is clearly expressed.

text: The card should use a unique diversified secret key, personalized into the card, to generate and authenticate transaction signatures
rationale: A unique card key generates and authenticates transaction signatures, which detect alteration and verify origin.

text: If this is not a cash load, the funds issuer needs to verify that the funds are requested by the legitimate account owner, which is normally done by the presentation of an enciphered PIN
rationale: Verifies that the requester is the legitimate account owner through an enciphered PIN.

text: The card issuer needs to ensure that the load acquirer is guaranteeing payment for the electronic value, and that the card is authentic
rationale: Requires ensuring that the card is authentic, which is authenticity of a component.

text: The load acquirer needs to ensure that the issuer is the true owner of the card, and, in the case of an apparent failure of the load, the load acquirer needs the card presented to authenticate the failure
rationale: Requires verifying that the issuer is the true owner of the card and authenticating the card, i.e. verification of identity.

text: The load device sends S1 in an authorization request to the issuer
rationale: Describes only a message flow (sending S1 in an authorization request) without stating a security property.

text: The load device also provides for verification of the identity of the cardholder (with either on-line or off-line PIN verification) and forwards verification data in the authorization request
rationale: Provides PIN-based verification of the cardholder's identity, which is authentication.

text: The issuer validates S1 to authenticate the card and the data to be used in the transaction
rationale: The issuer validates S1 to authenticate the card (authenticity) and the transaction data (data correctness).

text: The issuer sends S2 to the load acquirer in the authorization response message
rationale: Describes only the sending of S2 in a response message without stating a security property.

text: Unloads are permitted only to an account controlled by the card issuer and are performed only at a load device under the control of the card issuer
rationale: Restricts unloads to issuer-controlled accounts and devices, limiting who and where funds may be modified.

text: The cardholder must have an account relationship with the card issuer, and funds removed from the card are credited to the cardholder account only after the card issuer authenticates the card
rationale: Funds are credited only after the card issuer authenticates the card.

text: The issuer needs only to authenticate the card, and the card needs only to authenticate the issuer and that the data is the same as used by the issuer
rationale: Mutual authentication of card and issuer, and the card checks that the data is the same as the issuer's data (consistency).

text: The card generates S1, using data from the card and load device, and sends S1 to the card issuer to authenticate the card and the data that is to be used in the transaction
rationale: S1 is sent to authenticate the card and the data to be used in the transaction.

text: The card issuer generates S2, which is sent to the card to allow the card to validate the card issuer's authenticity and to ensure that the data used by the card in the transaction is the same as the card issuer intended
rationale: S2 lets the card validate the issuer's authenticity and ensures the transaction data is unchanged from what the issuer intended.

text: During a purchase transaction, the CEP card must ensure that it is dealing with an authentic POS device, and it must generate a signature to allow the card issuer to verify the integrity of the transaction
rationale: The card must verify the POS device is authentic and sign so the issuer can verify transaction integrity.

text: The POS device must ensure that it is dealing with an authentic card, and guarantee integrity of transactions and batches to the merchant acquirer
rationale: The POS device must ensure the card is authentic and guarantee integrity of transactions and batches.

text: In the case of a reversal, the CEP card must re-authenticate the PSAM
rationale: The card must re-authenticate the PSAM during a reversal.

text: The card must ensure that the transaction is performed by the same POS device as was used for the purchase being canceled, and that the amount of the cancellation is the same as the amount of the purchase, or, in the case of an incremental purchase, the same as the amount of the last step
rationale: Ensures the cancellation matches the original purchase device and amount, a data consistency check on the transaction.

text: During a Cancel Last Purchase transaction, the CEP card is authenticated by the PSAM in the POS device
rationale: The CEP card is authenticated by the PSAM.

text: The PSAM authenticates that the purchase transaction being canceled was performed by the PSAM, and that the transaction being canceled is part of the active batch
rationale: The PSAM authenticates the origin of the transaction being canceled and its membership in the active batch.

text: The card issuer and the merchant acquirer also authenticate the transaction when they receive it
rationale: The issuer and merchant acquirer authenticate the transaction upon receipt.

text: Transmissions between host systems should be protected by MACs based on unique keys that are shared by the nodes involved
rationale: MACs protect transmissions between hosts, which detects alteration of data.

text: The transaction signatures ensure end to end integrity of transmitted data for load, unload, and currency exchange transactions
rationale: Transaction signatures ensure end-to-end integrity of transmitted data.

text: These totals are used by the merchant acquirer to ensure the integrity of the batch
rationale: Batch totals are used by the merchant acquirer to ensure batch integrity.

text: The count and amount of the transactions in the batch must be protected by the S4 MAC, This information is not part of the card issuer's verification process
rationale: The batch count and amount must be protected by a MAC, which detects alteration.

text: Scheme providers must assign unique identifying numbers to merchant acquirers who provide PSAMs
rationale: Unique identifying numbers for merchant acquirers allow actions to be traced uniquely to an entity.

text: These merchant acquirers must then assign unique identifiers to PSAMs
rationale: Unique identifiers for each PSAM allow actions to be traced uniquely to the device.

text: Each PSAM must maintain a transaction count, The unique PSAM ID and the transaction count are used during a conversation with a CEP card. The transaction count must not be reset during the life of the PSAM
rationale: A unique PSAM ID and a never-reset transaction count give unique traceability of transactions to a device.

text: Contain the CA public RSA key, the PSAM's private RSA key and optionally the certificates that the POS device uses to perform mutual authentication with the CEP card
rationale: Holds keys and certificates used for mutual authentication between the POS device and the CEP card.

text: Perform the calculation required to generate a signature using the PSAM's private RSA key, to allow the CEP card to validate the PSAM
rationale: Generates a signature so the CEP card can validate the PSAM, verifying its identity.

text: Be the entity that maintains control over the flow of a transaction, ensuring that all security is enforced
rationale: Generic statement that all security is enforced, with no specific subcharacteristic stated.

text: Perform the verification of signatures and certificates during a purchase and cancel last purchase transaction
rationale: Verification of signatures and certificates checks the identity/origin of parties and the integrity of the signed data.

text: Ensure that CA public keys, aggregation parameters, blocking lists and issuer certificate revocation lists from the scheme providers are sent to the POS devices
rationale: Distributing CA public keys and certificate revocation lists supports verifying the validity of certificates, i.e. authenticity.

text: Share one or more MAC keys with connecting processors, create a MAC on each transmission sent to another processor, and verify the MAC on each transmission received from another processor
rationale: Creating and verifying a MAC on each transmission detects alteration and verifies the origin processor.

text: The scheme provider must ensure that the entire process between merchants, merchant acquirers, card issuers, and processors is auditable and reconcilable
rationale: An auditable and reconcilable end-to-end process implies traceability of who did what.

text: If errors in the card issuer MAC are discovered by the card issuer during its processing of the transactions, a dispute mechanism, established by the scheme provider, may be used to have money refunded
rationale: MAC errors indicate altered data and a dispute mechanism provides a means to contest transactions, with weak evidentiary flavor.

text: If a scheme provider establishes a central error repository, all transactions for the scheme with MAC errors must be sent to that central error repository whether or not they are submitted to the dispute process
rationale: Collecting all transactions with MAC errors in a central repository concerns handling detected data-integrity failures.

text: A purchase transaction may be reversed, prior to the removal of the CEP card from the POS device, by sending a purchase reversal command to the CEP card, The CEP card must authenticate the PSAM using certificates previously exchanged
rationale: The card must authenticate the PSAM using previously exchanged certificates.

text: The amount to be reversed is the amount of the last step of the transaction. The reversal command sent to the CEP card contains a S2 MAC computed by the PSAM
rationale: The reversal command carries a MAC computed by the PSAM, protecting the command against alteration.

text: The PSAM in the POS device generates a merchant acquirer S5 MAC for the transaction, computes a new S4 MAC on the updated batch total count and amount, and logs the transaction
rationale: MACs on the transaction and batch totals protect integrity, and the transaction is logged.

text: The CEP card authenticates the PSAM using the certificates previously received and the S2, The CEP card increments the value of the purse and logs the transaction
rationale: The card authenticates the PSAM via certificates and logs the transaction.

text: The CEP card verifies that the PSAM is the PSAM used in the original transaction, computes a S1 MAC using the same DES session key that was used for the purchase transaction being cancelled, and responds to the POS device with the S1 and the identification of the last transaction. If the purchase transaction to be canceled has been canceled or is not part of the active batch, the command is not allowed
rationale: The card verifies the PSAM identity and returns a MAC, and the command is disallowed for already cancelled or out-of-batch transactions.

text: The PSAM either retrieves or re-derives the DES session key used for the purchase transaction being cancelled. The POS device authenticates the CEP card using this key and the S1 MAC
rationale: The POS device authenticates the CEP card using the session key and the S1 MAC.

text: The PSAM in the POS device generates a merchant acquirer S5 MAC for the transaction and a new S4 MAC for the batch total count and amount and logs the transaction. The amount of the canceled last purchase transaction is subtracted from the header amount. The transaction is kept in a data store associated with the POS device until the merchant acquirer collects it
rationale: MACs protect the transaction and batch totals and the transaction is logged and retained for collection.

text: A credit command, which contains the S2 MAC computed by the PSAM using the session key, is sent to the CEP card
rationale: The credit command includes a MAC computed with the session key, protecting it against alteration.

text: The CEP card authenticates the terminal using the S2 MAC and the session key from the purchase transaction being cancelled. The CEP card increments the value of the purse and logs the transaction. The CEP card verifies that the cancellation amount is equal to the amount of the last step of the purchase transaction
rationale: The card authenticates the terminal via the MAC, logs the transaction, and verifies the cancellation amount matches.

text: A transaction collection process must exist. Data being transmitted from the POS devices must be transmitted in a manner that ensures integrity of the data
rationale: Transmitted data must be sent in a manner that ensures its integrity.

text: Each POS transaction completed at the POS device is given a S5 MAC by the PSAM, which is used by the merchant acquirer to validate that the transactions were made at a POS device with a valid PSAM. The batch total count and amount must be protected by the S4 MAC, which must also be validated by the merchant acquirer
rationale: MACs validate that transactions came from a valid PSAM and protect the batch totals from alteration.

text: The merchant acquirer validates the PSAM's MACs prior to accepting the POS transactions for payment. In addition, selected data elements are validated to ensure correct processing by the POS device and its PSAM
rationale: The acquirer validates PSAM MACs and data elements before accepting transactions, checking origin and correctness.

text: Each purchase transaction is signed by the CEP card with a S6 MAC, which is used by the card issuer to validate that the transaction was made with a legitimate, not counterfeit, CEP card. The card issuer validates the CEP card's MAC
rationale: The card signs each transaction with a MAC so the issuer can validate it came from a legitimate, non-counterfeit card.

text: Payment decisions are based on signature validations, scheme provider rules, and merchant and merchant acquirer agreements
rationale: Payment decisions depend on signature validation, which checks integrity and origin.

text: Pay on detail is the default payment arrangement for merchant acquirers to provide payment to their merchants. In this arrangement, the merchant acquirer relies on the POS transaction S5 MAC to determine acceptance. Merchants are paid only for valid POS transactions
rationale: Acceptance is determined by relying on the validity of the POS transaction MAC.

text: All load transactions are on-line transactions. Authorization of funds for load transactions must require a form of cardholder verification. The load device must support on-line encrypted PIN or off-line PIN verification
rationale: Cardholder verification via PIN is required, with encrypted online PIN protecting the PIN from disclosure.

text: Off-line PIN verification must include both encrypted and unencrypted PIN
rationale: Off-line PIN verification is a cardholder authentication method, with encrypted PIN implying protection against disclosure.

text: The card verification method indicator (CVMI) in the CEP card must specify support of online PIN verification and at least one method of off-line PIN verification (encrypted or unencrypted)
rationale: The card must specify supported PIN verification methods for cardholder verification.

text: Since these transactions are on-line to the issuer, the issuer has the opportunity to lock the card or the application. These transactions are not available to a card that has already been locked
rationale: The issuer can lock a card or application and locked cards cannot transact, a containment measure against misuse.

text: Only one version of the CA public key is required in the card. This requires that the PSAMs with which the CEP card exchanges cryptograms must be capable of generating and validating cryptograms using the relevant keys from all current cards
rationale: PSAMs must generate and validate cryptograms with the relevant keys, supporting verification of card and terminal identity.

text: Two-way, or mutual, authentication, where the card authenticates the terminal and the terminal authenticates the card for each transaction, must be performed for off-line transactions
rationale: Mutual authentication between card and terminal is required for off-line transactions.

text: For increased security and convenience, asymmetric cryptography must be used as the authentication security for off-line transactions
rationale: Asymmetric cryptography must be used as the authentication mechanism for off-line transactions.

text: The card must authenticate the terminal at the point of sale, ensuring that it is genuine and valid, and use a two-way authentication process
rationale: The card must authenticate the terminal as genuine using two-way authentication.

text: The terminal must authenticate the card and the transaction at the point of sale, ensuring that they are genuine and valid
rationale: The terminal must authenticate the card and transaction as genuine and valid.

text: The terminal must participate in a two-way authentication process with the card
rationale: Two-way authentication between terminal and card is mutual identity verification.

text: For cancel last purchase transactions, the terminal must validate the card and sign the cancellation
rationale: Validating the card verifies identity and signing the cancellation protects the transaction against alteration.

text: The terminal must secure transactions by retaining the card's symmetric MACing key signature as part of the transaction
rationale: Retaining the MAC signature with the transaction secures it by allowing detection of alteration.

text: The terminal must generate a symmetric MACing key signature and send it to the merchant acquirer
rationale: Generating a MAC and sending it to the acquirer lets alteration be detected, with no explicit proof or origin claim.

text: Incremental purchase transactions must use two-way authentication for the initial session authentication, and at least one-way, with the terminal authenticating the card, for the remaining increments or some of the remaining increments
rationale: Requires two-way or one-way authentication of the card and terminal during incremental purchases.

text: Load and unload functions must be authenticated using end-to-end security between the card and the card issuer
rationale: Load and unload functions must be authenticated end to end between card and issuer.

text: The issuer host must authenticate the card upon the load/unload request
rationale: The issuer host must authenticate the card, which is identity verification.

text: The card must authenticate the issuer host upon the response to the request
rationale: The card must authenticate the issuer host, which is identity verification.

text: A proof must be sent to the load acquirer that a load or unload occurred to avoid repudiation
rationale: A proof of the load or unload is required explicitly to avoid repudiation.

text: The management of keys must be accomplished in a secure, certified environment
rationale: Generic secure environment for key management without a specific subcharacteristic stated.

text: There may be multiple certification authorities that manage keys for the system, including the possibility of one overall highest level certification authority (perhaps on an international level), and domestic certification authorities for each country or region
rationale: Describes the organization of certification authorities without stating a security property.

text: The system must protect the integrity of key transaction data including transaction identification, currency code and amount. If tampering is suspected, the system must cause the transaction to fail
rationale: Protects transaction data integrity and makes the transaction fail when tampering is suspected.

text: Funds issuers must accept funds authorization requests, regardless of the load currency type, as permitted
rationale: Functional requirement about accepting authorization requests in any currency, not a security property.

text: Authorizations for load transactions require a form of cardholder authentication for funds requests
rationale: Load authorizations require cardholder authentication.

text: The load device must support on-line PIN encryption or off-line PIN verification
rationale: PIN encryption protects the PIN from disclosure and PIN verification authenticates the cardholder.

text: The load device which supports only off-line PIN verification must support both the off-line PIN encryption method and the off-line PIN plain text verification method as defined in EMV
rationale: Off-line PIN encryption and verification methods protect the PIN and verify the cardholder.

text: Unload transactions do not require cardholder authentication. (However, an acquirer's devices may be configured such that authentication is required for access.)
rationale: States that unload does not require cardholder authentication, so it imposes no authentication demand.

text: All applications under the GlobalPlatform shall be implemented in a hardware-neutral secure runtime environment
rationale: Generic secure runtime environment without a specific stated property.

text: The run time environment shall be responsible to separate secure storage for the application code and data
rationale: Separate secure storage for application code and data protects them from disclosure and unauthorized modification.

text: Security domain shall ensure complete seperation of keys among the card issuers and other application providers
rationale: Complete separation of keys among providers limits access to keys to their owners.

text: " ""Security Domains shall support security services such as key handling, encryption, decryption, digital signature generation and verification for their providers' such as card issuer, applicaiton providers and controlling authority"""
rationale: Encryption/decryption services support confidentiality and digital signature generation and verification support integrity.

text: The OPEN shall responsible to enforce security principles defined for Card Content management.
rationale: Generic enforcement of security principles with no specific subcharacteristic named.

text: The GlobalPlatform API shall provides services to the application such as card verification and security services
rationale: Card verification services imply verifying the card's identity, while the other security services are unspecified.

text: The primary goal of the GlobalPlatform is to ensure the security and integrity of the card's components for the life of the card. These components are The runtime environment,The OPEN,The Issuer Security Domain,Supplementary Security Domains, The Applications.
rationale: The goal explicitly includes ensuring the integrity of the card's components.

text: To ensure card security and integrity, the GlobalPlatform is designed to support a range of secure mechanisms for: Data integrity, Resource availability, Confidentiality, Authentication.
rationale: Lists data integrity, confidentiality and authentication mechanisms; resource availability is out of scope.

text: The Card Issuer is responsible for Generating and loading the Issuer Security Domain keys,
rationale: Assigns responsibility for generating and loading keys without stating a security property.

text: " ""The Card Issuer is responsible for Enforcing standards and policies for Application Providers governing all aspects of Applications to be provided to the Card Issuer or operated on the Card Issuer's cards,"""
rationale: Generic policy enforcement responsibility of the issuer with no specific subcharacteristic.

text: The Card Issuer is responsible for Cryptographically authorizing load, install, and extradition to be performed by Application Providers.
rationale: Cryptographic authorization of load, install and extradition by providers implies verifiable authorization of the origin.

text: " ""The Application Provider is responsible for Generating the keys for its own Security Domains or obtaining Security Domain keys from a trusted third party,"""
rationale: Assigns responsibility for generating or obtaining keys without stating a security property.

text: The Application Provider is responsible for Working with the Card Issuer to load generated keys into the Application Provider's Security Domain,
rationale: Loading generated keys into a Security Domain is a key-provisioning duty that does not clearly state any of the six subcharacteristics.

text: " ""The Application Provider is responsible for Providing load file data block signatures according to its own security policy for integrity and source authenticity,"""
rationale: Load file data block signatures are explicitly provided for integrity and source authenticity.

text: " ""A Controlling Authority is responsible for Generating the keys for its own Security Domain or obtaining Security Domain keys from a trusted third party,"""
rationale: Generating or obtaining Security Domain keys is key management without an explicit security property stated.

text: A Controlling Authority is responsible for Working with the Card Issuer to load generated keys into the Controlling Authority's Security Domain,
rationale: Working with the Card Issuer to load keys is a key-provisioning duty with no explicit subcharacteristic.

text: " ""A Controlling Authority is responsible for Providing load file data block signatures according to its own security policy for integrity and source authenticity."""
rationale: Load file data block signatures are explicitly provided for integrity and source authenticity.

text: " ""The runtime environment is responsible for Providing an interface to all Applications that ensures that the runtime environment security mechanisms cannot be bypassed, deactivated, corrupted or otherwise circumvented,"""
rationale: Security mechanisms must not be bypassed, deactivated, corrupted or circumvented, which is resistance to attack.

text: The runtime environment is responsible for Performing secure memory management
rationale: Generic statement of secure memory management with no specific property stated.

text: " ""Secure memory management shall ensure that Each application's code and data (including transient session data) as well as the runtime environment itself and its data (including transient session data) is protected from unauthorized access from within the card,"""
rationale: Code and data must be protected from unauthorized access, covering both reading and modification.

text: " ""Secure memory management shall ensure that When more than one logical channel is supported, each concurrently selected Application's code and data (including transient session data) as well as the runtime environment itself and its data (including transient session data) is protected from unauthorized access from within the card,"""
rationale: Each concurrently selected application's code and data must be protected from unauthorized access, covering both reading and modification.

text: Secure memory management shall ensure that The previous contents of the memory is not accessible when that memory is reused,
rationale: Previous memory contents must not be accessible on reuse, which prevents disclosure of data.

text: " ""Secure memory management shall ensure that The memory recovery process is secure and consistent in case of a loss of power or withdrawal of the card from the card reader while an operation is in progress,"""
rationale: Memory recovery must be secure and consistent after power loss or card withdrawal, which preserves data consistency.

text: " ""The runtime environment is responsible for Providing communication services with off-card entities that ensures the proper transmission (according to the specific communication protocol rules) of unaltered command and response messages."""
rationale: Command and response messages must be transmitted unaltered.

text: Each Trusted Framework present on the card shall Check the application access rules of the inter-acting Applications according to their respective privileges,
rationale: Checking application access rules by privilege is access control over what applications may read or modify.

text: " ""Each Trusted Framework present on the card shall Enforce the Trusted Framework security rules for inter-application communication, including the rules, defined in appendix G,"""
rationale: Enforcing unspecified inter-application security rules does not state a specific property.

text: Each Trusted Framework present on the card shall Ensure that incoming messages are properly routed unaltered to their intended destinations,
rationale: Incoming messages must be routed unaltered.

text: " ""Each Trusted Framework present on the card shall Ensure that any response messages are properly returned unaltered (except for any cryptographic protection) to the original receiver of the incoming message."""
rationale: Response messages must be returned unaltered to the original receiver.

text: " ""The OPEN shall Provide an interface to all Applications that ensures that the GlobalPlatform security mechanism cannot be bypassed, deactivated, corrupted or otherwise circumvented,"""
rationale: The security mechanism must not be bypassed, deactivated, corrupted or circumvented, which is resistance to attack.

text: The OPEN shall Check application access rules according to the Applications' privileges,
rationale: Checking application access rules by privilege is access control over what applications may read or modify.

text: The OPEN shall Ensure that the Card Content changes are authorized by the Card Issuer,
rationale: Card Content changes must be authorized by the Card Issuer, which restricts who can modify content.

text: The OPEN shall Ensure that application code has been signed by the Controlling Authority represented on the card,
rationale: Checking the Controlling Authority's signature on application code detects alteration and verifies its origin.

text: The OPEN shall Ensure that application code has been signed by Application Providers represented on the card, if required.
rationale: Checking the Application Provider's signature on application code detects alteration and verifies its origin.

text: Security Domains enforce the security policies of their off-card Security Domain Provider.
rationale: Enforcing the provider's unspecified security policies does not state a specific property.

text: " ""When applicable a Security Domain shall Communicate with off-card entities in accordance with its Security Domain Provider's security policy in Pre-Issuance and Post-Issuance,"""
rationale: Communicating per the provider's security policy refers to an unspecified policy with no explicit property.

text: When applicable a Security Domain shall Manage on-card data securely,
rationale: Managing on-card data securely is generic and does not specify confidentiality or integrity.

text: " ""When applicable a Security Domain shall Provide cryptographic protection services for its own Applications during their personalization and optionally during their subsequent operation,"""
rationale: Cryptographic protection services for applications imply protecting data, although the property is not detailed.

text: When applicable a Security Domain shall Verify the authorization for Card Content changes initiated by an off-card authority,
rationale: Verifying authorization for Card Content changes restricts who can modify content.

text: When applicable a Security Domain shall Verify the load file data block signature when requested by the OPEN.
rationale: Verifying the load file data block signature detects alteration and checks its origin.

text: A Global Services Application shall Hold the Global Services application-related data securely,
rationale: Holding data securely is generic and does not specify confidentiality or integrity.

text: A Global Services Application shall Perform internal security measures as required by the service.
rationale: Unspecified internal security measures do not state a specific property.

text: Applications should Expose only data and resources that are necessary for proper application functionality
rationale: Exposing only necessary data limits disclosure of information, which fits Confidentiality.

text: Applications should Perform internal security measures required by the Application Provider
rationale: Generic requirement for unspecified internal security measures, so no subcharacteristic is clearly expressed.

text: The back-end systems (multiple back-end systems may exist for a single card), which communicate with the cards, perform the verifications, and manage the off-card key databases, also shall be trusted.
rationale: Only states that back-end systems must be trusted without naming a specific security property.

text: " ""One of the major requirements for a GlobalPlatform card is the ability to provide a minimum level of cryptographic functionality. This cryptography is, for example, used for the generation of signatures, and is available for use by the Applications present on the card."""
rationale: Describes a generic cryptographic capability without stating which security property it serves.

text: The Issuer Security Domain shall implement one Secure Channel Protocol.
rationale: Requires a secure channel protocol, which by rule 5 maps to Confidentiality, with no explicit mention of alteration detection.

text: A Security Domain other than the Issuer Security Domain shall implement [at least] one Secure Channel Protocol.
rationale: Requires a secure channel protocol, which by rule 5 maps to Confidentiality, with no explicit mention of alteration detection.

text: A GlobalPlatform card should support symmetric cryptography such as the Data Encryption Standard (DES) algorithm.
rationale: Support for symmetric encryption such as DES points to protecting data from disclosure.

text: A GlobalPlatform card may also support asymmetric cryptography such as the Rivest / Shamir / Adleman (RSA) algorithm.
rationale: Optional asymmetric cryptography such as RSA is an encryption capability aimed at data confidentiality.

text: When present, services to encrypt and decrypt any pattern of data using these algorithms shall be available to Applications.
rationale: Encryption and decryption services for application data serve data confidentiality.

text: " ""It is the responsibility of the Card Issuer or the Controlling Authority to set up the appropriate off-card procedures to comply with the governmental restrictions upon cryptography. Features to disable or restrict cryptography usage by Applications on a card are beyond the scope of this Specification."""
rationale: Concerns regulatory responsibility and scope limits for cryptography, not a security property of the system.

text: The Load File Data Block Hash is intended to verify the integrity of a complete Load File Data Block when loaded to a GlobalPlatform card.
rationale: The hash is explicitly meant to verify the integrity of the loaded data block.

text: The Load File Data Block Hash is used in the computation of The Load File Data Block Signature
rationale: A hash feeding a signature computation is an alteration-detection mechanism, matching Integrity under rule 4.

text: When present during the loading of a Load File to the card, each signature shall be verified by the appropriate Security Domain.
rationale: Signature verification on loaded files detects alteration (Integrity), while the text does not state that origin or identity is verified.

text: Tokens shall be verified by the appropriate Security Domain.
rationale: Verification of tokens by the Security Domain is a credential check, which fits Authenticity.

text: A GlobalPlatform card offers Entity authentication - in which the card or the off-card entity proves its authenticity to the other entity through a cryptographic exchange,
rationale: Entities prove their authenticity to each other through a cryptographic exchange, which is entity authentication.

text: A GlobalPlatform card offers Integrity and authentication - in which the receiving entity (the card or off-card entity) ensures that the data being received from the sending entity (respectively the off-card entity or card) actually came from an authenticated entity in the correct sequence and has not been altered,
rationale: Ensures data came from an authenticated entity and has not been altered, covering Authenticity and Integrity.

text: A GlobalPlatform card offers Confidentiality - in which data being transmitted from the sending entity (the off-card entity or card) to the receiving entity (respectively the card or off-card entity) is not viewable by an unauthenticated entity.
rationale: Transmitted data must not be viewable by an unauthenticated entity, which is Confidentiality.

text: The life cycle models is responsible to functionality and security of Card, Executable Load Files, Executable Modules, Security Domains, and Applications.
rationale: Vague statement that life cycle models are responsible for functionality and security, with no specific property.

text: The OPEN shall be responsible to maintain security and administration of the card and its content
rationale: Generic responsibility to maintain security and administration without naming a specific property.

text: The off-card entity under the OP_READY state may insert Security Domain keys in order to maintain a cryptographic key separation from the Issuer Security Domain keys
rationale: Describes key separation as a key-management option without explicitly stating a protected property or attack.

text: The SECURED state may be used to enforce the relevant security policies of the security domain and applications
rationale: Generic enforcement of security policies by a life cycle state, with no specific property stated.

text: The off-card entity under the SECURE state shall be used to ensure the availability of all keys by the issuer security domain
rationale: Concerns availability of keys, which is not a security subcharacteristic per rule 9.

text: Internally to the CPN, a CNG transmitting private or other critical information (i.e. to a CND) shall protect the data from unauthorised disclosure.
rationale: Private or critical information must be protected from unauthorised disclosure.

text: Internally to the CPN, a CNG receiving private or other critical information (i.e. from a CND) should verify that the data was protected from unauthorised disclosure.
rationale: The receiver verifies that data was protected from unauthorised disclosure, which concerns Confidentiality.

text: The CNG shall detect the end of the life of the key used for cryptographic protection of the wireless communication between the CND and the CNG.
rationale: Detecting key end of life is key lifecycle management and does not explicitly state a protected property or attack.

text: A CPN-user attempting to invoke a CNG-mediated service shall be identified and authenticated by the CNG before being granted access to the service.
rationale: Users must be identified and authenticated before accessing a service, which is Authenticity.

text: The CNG shall implement an authentication failure handling policy.
rationale: An authentication failure handling policy addresses repeated or failed access attempts, which fits Resistance, though the text gives no detail.

text: The CNG shall take action according to local authentication failure handling policy (which may include silently discarding the authentication and explicit failure notification, or in the case of a replay of credentials may include notification of the true owner of the credentials) upon detection of failure during identification, authentication and authorization.
rationale: Handles failures of identification and authentication, including credential replay, covering Authenticity and Resistance.

text: The CNG should detect replayed user and/or device credentials.
rationale: Detecting replayed credentials is replay-attack detection, which is Resistance.

text: When the CNG detects replayed user and/or device credentials, the CNG shall stop the relevant processes.
rationale: Detecting replayed credentials and stopping processes is resistance to a replay attack.

text: The CNG shall implement a privacy protection policy specifying as a minimum private and critical information.
rationale: A privacy protection policy covering private and critical information is about preventing disclosure.

text: When the CNG detects violation of the privacy protection policy the CNG shall discard all signalling, including signalling from the NGN.
rationale: Discarding signalling upon a privacy policy violation enforces privacy, with no explicit attack mentioned.

text: The CNG shall implement an authorization management handling policy.
rationale: A generic authorization management policy does not state what is read, modified or attacked.

text: On reception at the CNG of a message to access configuration information for update and detection of authorization failure the CNG shall reject the request and manage the failure in accordance with the CPN authorization management handling policy.
rationale: Rejecting unauthorized requests to update configuration information restricts who can modify data.

text: Where a CND invokes a session at the CNG the CNG shall record the association of session-id, invoking device identity and invoking user-id.
rationale: Recording session, device identity and user id associates actions with their originator for traceability.

text: On transmission of management information from the CNG to a CND the CNG shall append a timestamp or sequence number to the outgoing message.
rationale: Appending a timestamp or sequence number is a replay-protection mechanism, though replay is not named here.

text: On reception at the CNG of a message containing management information the CNG shall extract the timestamp or sequence number and verify that the message has not been replayed.
rationale: Verifying the message has not been replayed explicitly counters replay attacks.

text: On reception at the CNG of a message to access or update configuration information the CNG shall allow access only if the sender is an administrator.
rationale: Allowing access to view or update configuration only to administrators is role-based access control for reading and modifying.

text: On detection of a message integrity error at the CNG the CNG shall discard the message.
rationale: Discarding a message on detecting an integrity error is alteration detection.

text: On indication received at the CNG of a resource allocation expiry the CNG shall delete all residual data associated with the invocation of the resource.
rationale: Deleting residual data after resource expiry prevents leftover data from being disclosed.

text: On receipt of a valid (i.e. authorized) request for data stored in the CNG the CNG shall return the requested data to the requesting user.
rationale: Data is returned only for authorized requests, which restricts reading to authorized users.

text: On receipt of a valid (i.e. authorized) request for access to a CNG hosted service or application the CNG shall provide the requested service or application to the requesting user.
rationale: Providing a service to authorized requests is access to a service, with no data read or modification restriction stated.

text: On detection of any system failure or discontinuity not specifically handled by other mechanisms the CNG shall revert to a known safe state.
rationale: Reverting to a known safe state on failure is a secure failure state, though failures are not stated as malicious.

text: The CNG shall support mechanisms to authenticate itself to the NGN for connectivity purposes.
rationale: The CNG authenticating itself to the NGN is identity verification.

text: The CNG shall support mechanisms to authenticate itself to the NGN for service usage purposes.
rationale: The CNG authenticating itself to the NGN for service usage is identity verification.

text: The CNG shall support mechanisms to authenticate CNDs to the NGN for service usage purposes if they are not able to fully support the related procedures in an autonomous way.
rationale: Authenticating CNDs to the NGN is device authentication.

text: The CNG shall support mechanisms for authentication of wireless CNDs for local connectivity. Similar mechanisms may be also implemented for non-wireless devices.
rationale: Authentication of wireless devices for local connectivity is device authentication.

text: The CNG and CPN shall support mechanisms that prevent access to the network by unauthorized users.
rationale: Preventing network access by unauthorized users is access restriction, with no explicit data read or write scope.

text: The capacity of the authorized entities should depend on the security policies defined by the service providers, managing the CNG.
rationale: Capacity of authorized entities depending on provider security policy is generic and fits no subcharacteristic clearly.

text: The CNG and the CPN shall implement mechanisms to limit the visibility of the WAN side network and resources to authorized entities.
rationale: Limiting visibility of WAN side resources to authorized entities restricts access to information.

text: The diagnostic operations on the CPN by an operator shall be performed in accordance with rules protecting the users' privacy.
rationale: Rules protecting users' privacy during diagnostics concern privacy.

text: CPN environment shall be protected with a stateful firewall function, that may be implemented in the CNG.
rationale: A stateful firewall protects the network against intrusions and hostile traffic.

text: The CNG and the CPN shall be able to support parental control related functionalities limiting the use of the broadband connection on a user or time basis. Limitations on a content basis may be shared with devoted network servers.
rationale: Parental control limiting connection use is a usage restriction, not a security subcharacteristic.
